This lack of top-line momentum is further underscored by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of -24%, indicating a long-term structural decline [E11]. Furthermore, the business is currently failing to generate positive earnings, as reflected in a negative P/E ratio of -2.13x and a recent 7% decline in trailing twelve-month profit growth [E4, E16, E38]. The bear’s focus on stagnant sales [E11, E12, E13, E14] ignores the company’s ability to maintain profitability, as evidenced by a 11% compounded profit growth over the last five years [E15]. While the bear highlights negative returns [E6, E8], the market is clearly pricing in a turnaround or asset-based recovery, as the stock is currently trading at the absolute top of its 52-week range [E3]. Despite these headwinds, the current market momentum [E3] suggests that investors are looking past the historical sales decline toward a potential inflection point. The bear's reliance on trailing metrics [E16, E38] fails to account for the market's current bullish sentiment, which is actively bidding the stock to its yearly high [E3].

The bull’s reliance on a 11% profit growth figure [E15] is misleading, as it ignores the most recent evidence showing that profit growth has already decelerated to -7% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E38]. While the bull interprets the stock price hitting its 52-week high [E3] as a sign of a turnaround, this momentum is disconnected from the fundamental reality of a company with a -21.13% ROCE [E8] and a -19.28% ROA [E6], both of which significantly underperform their sector benchmarks. The bull’s optimism regarding a potential inflection point is contradicted by a decade-long trend of -24% compounded sales growth [E11]. Furthermore, the negative P/E ratio [E4] and the complete lack of dividend yield [E2] confirm that investors are not being compensated for the risk of holding a business that is failing to generate top-line growth [E14]. Ultimately, the market price [E3] is not a substitute for the underlying operational decay evidenced by the company's inability to grow sales [E13] or maintain positive returns on capital [E8].
